t: Software That Writes Its Tests Systems Simulator
title: Software That Writes Its Tests Systems Simulator
definition: Simulates Software That Writes Its Tests operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Software That Writes Its Tests installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 44417 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where test synthesizers monitoring, software logistics redundancy, or coverage goals maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

t: Software That Writes Its Tests Master Roadmap
title: Software That Writes Its Tests Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Software That Writes Its Tests: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Software That Writes Its Tests — systems generating their own test suites.

Phase 1 — Prove (test synthesizers): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (software logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (coverage goals): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (mutation testing): software hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and developers-scale deployment begins.

Signature edition: phases overlap aggressively — integration starts on day one. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.

Each phase has exit criteria.
